Hi Alex / Maria —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a hosted pricing proposal that matches your operational profile. I recorded the call and exported a short traffic sample (attached). Please confirm the bolded numbers below if they look right: 

TL;DR (please confirm):
- Expected steady-state monthly token consumption: ~9,200,000 tokens (9.2M)
- Monthly variability: +/- ~15% (week-to-week seasonality)
- 99th-percentile sustained throughput: ~180 requests/sec (TPS)
- Short spikes observed during batch jobs: up to ~260 TPS for <5 minutes
- Target unit economics for procurement: ~$50 per 1M tokens
- Ballpark budget for hosted API: ~$350–$550 / month (targeting ~$460/mo at stated unit price)

Questions / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the numbers above (steady-state, variability, 99th/peak TPS)?
2) Do you expect a firm committed monthly token number (e.g., 9M committed) vs purely consumption invoicing?
3) Any procurement constraints on billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) or required invoicing terms?

If those numbers are correct I can ask our pricing lead for a committed-usage proposal (we typically layer a volume/commit discount) and a hosted plan that supports the short 260 TPS bursts with autoscaling.

Attachments: traffic_snapshot.csv (sample minute-level token counts), call_recording_20260524.mp3

Thanks — I’ll hold until you confirm the numbers and preference for committed vs consumption.

Thanks Grace — confirm those numbers look correct based on what I ran this morning against our telemetry. A few clarifications: 

- Steady-state: 9.2M tokens/month is our conservative forecast for Q3. We could see +/–15% like you noted.
- Peak profile: 99th ~180 TPS is accurate; spikes to ~260 TPS are rare and tied to an ingestion window we run nightly for 3–4 minutes. We can tolerate a short soft-threshold breach if the provider supports short bursts without throttling.
- Procurement: we prefer a committed monthly baseline (9M) with an overage pay-as-you-go model.
- Target $/1M: procurement would like $50 / 1M as a target for negotiations. If you have tiered discounts for commit that would be great to see.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing is preferred; Net-30 is our standard but willing to discuss.

Please proceed with a committed-hosted proposal that surfaces a committed price for 9M tokens + overage pricing and call out whether short bursts to 260 TPS are covered by the hosted plan (or whether we need dedicated capacity).

Appreciate it — Alex

Forwarding Alex's confirmation. Key asks from the customer: committed baseline ~9M tokens / month with overage, target $50 per 1M, support for 260 TPS short bursts (they want hosted if possible).

Can you put together two quick options I can send them by EOD: 
A) Committed-hosted option (monthly commit = 9M tokens): list unit price / 1M, overage price, expected monthly cost at list and at proposed discount. Note: procurement wants $50/1M as target — propose something competitive (include annual vs quarterly commit tiers).
B) Hosted + burst SLA note: confirm whether our hosted tier can absorb 260 TPS for <5 minute bursts without requiring Dedicated, and any soft request limits or throttling behavior. If hosted cannot guarantee, indicate which Dedicated configuration (GPU pool size) would be recommended and a rough delta in $/1M equivalent.

Attachments: pricing_model.csv, proposal_template_v2.docx (use proposal template to draft).

Thanks — I’ll include the customer in the thread when we have a clean option.

Thanks for the context — I reviewed the traffic sample. Quick take:

- Capacity: Hosted tier can tolerate 180 TPS 99th natively. We cover short bursts up to ~250 TPS via autoscaling and prefix/KV caching behavior; 260 TPS sustained for <5 min should be OK but I'll call this an engineering-dependent burst. We should call out a soft limit and offer a fallback to Dedicated if they require formal SLA on sustained 260 TPS.
- Pricing proposal (draft):
  * Quarterly commit (9M/month): $48 per 1M tokens (5% commit discount on published hosted list) → est. $441 / month at committed usage
  * Annual commit (9M/month): $45 per 1M tokens (10% commit discount) → est. $414 / month at committed usage
  * Overage: published hosted list price $60 / 1M tokens (billed pro rata)

Recommend we present both the quarterly and annual commit lines and surface the hosted burst caveat. I’ll create a quick quote in HubSpot and link it here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765 — please review the numbers and I’ll polish wording for procurement.
